Q1. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 Assam PSC AE (IWT) 14.03.2021 Oil India Limited Sr. Engineer (Drilling) 30.11.2019 KPCL AE 2016 MPPSC State Forest Service Exam, 2014
The forces, which meet at one point and their lines of action also lie on the same plane, are known as
A coplanar concurrent forces
✓ Correct Answer
B coplanar non-concurrent forces
C non-coplanar concurrent forces
D non-coplanar non-concurrent forces
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
Coplanar Concurrent Forces–The forces which meet at one point and their lines of action also lie on the same plane, are called coplanar concurrent forces. Coplanar Non-Concurrent Forces–The forces which do not meet at one point but their lines action lie on the same plane are known as coplanar non-concurrent forces. Non-Coplanar Concurrent Forces–The forces which meet at one point but their line of action do not lie on the same plane are known as non coplanar concurrent forces. Non Coplanar Non Concurrent Forces–The forces which do not meet at one point and their line of actions also do not lie on the same plane.
Q2. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 CGPSC AE 15.01.2021 Rajasthan Nagar Nigam AE 2016, Shift-II VIZAG STEEL MT - 2011
Non coplanar concurrent forces are those where
A All forces do not lie in one plane and their lines of action intersect at more than one point
B All forces are parallel to each other and lie in single plane
C All forces do not lie in one plane but their lines of action pass through one point
✓ Correct Answer
D All forces lie in one plane but their lines of action pass through one point
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
Non Coplanar Forces : Those forces which are not acting from a same plane. Concurrent Forces– A set of points forces is considered concurrent if all the lines of action of those forces meet come together at single point. Coplanar Forces–Those forces which are acting in same plane.

Q22. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 HPPSC Poly. Lect. 05.07.2021
The resultant of two forces P and Q is R. If one of the forces is reversed in direction, the resultant is S. Then for the identity R2 + S2 = 2 (P2 + Q2) to hold good,

Given, R P Q = +    .....(i) After reversing direction of one force (Q) we get S  = P Q −   .....(ii) Let angle between P & Q be θ So, resultant R2 = P2 + Q2 + 2PQcosθ .....(iii) Engineering Mechanics 19 YCT S2 = P2 + (–Q)2 – 2PQcosθ .....(iv) Adding equation (iii) & (iv) ( ) 2 2 2 2 R S 2 P Q + = + So, the identity does not depends on angle θ. Hence, forces can have any angle of inclination (θ) between them.

Q33. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 100 N, 200 N Oil India Senior Officer 23.12.2020
The resultant of two forces, one of which is double the other is 260 N. If the direction of the larger force is reversed and the other remain unaltered, the magnitude of the resultant reduces to 180 N. Determine the magnitude of the forces.
A 50 N, 200 N
B 50 N, 100 N
C 300 N, 100 N
D 100 N, 200 N
✓ Correct Answer
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
Let the forces be of magnitude P & 2P then, P2 + (2P)2 + 2P × 2Pcosθ = (260)2 .....(i) And similarly when larger force is reversed P2 + (–2P)2 + 2(P) (–2P)cosθ = (180)2 P2 + 4P2 – 4P2cosθ = (180)2 .....(ii) Adding equation (i) & (ii) 2P2 + 8P2 = 2602 + 1802 10P2 = 100000 P2 = 10000 P = 100 Larger force = 2P = 200 Hence, magnitude of the forces are 100 N & 200 N.

Q99. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 WBPSC AE 2003

Resultant– Resultant of a force system is a force or a couple that will have the same effect to the body both in translation and rotation, if all the forces are removed and replaced by the resultant. Rx → The x – component of the resultant is equal to the sum of forces in the x-direction. Ry → The y – component of the resultant is equal to the sum of forces in y-direction. Rx = ΣFx = 1 2 3 x x x F F F ...... + + + 1 2 3 y y y y y R F F F F ...... = ∑ = + + + 1 2 3 z z z z z R F F F F ...... = ∑ = + + + x x y 4 R F R F = ∑ = ∑ 2 2 x y x R R R H 0 F = + ∑ = = ∑ ∵ 2 y 0 R = + y R R = So, the resultant of the system can be a force vertically upward or downward.

Q203. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 MECON MT 2019 HPPSC Asstt. Prof. 29.10.2016 HPPSC Lect. (Auto) 23.04.2016 UKPSC AE 2012 Paper-I VIZAG Steel MT 2011 UKPSC AE 2007 Paper-I

A limiting friction
✓ Correct Answer
B static friction
C dynamic friction
D none of these
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
Limiting friction– The maximum friction that can be generated between two static surfaces in contact with each other. Once a force applied to the surfaces exceeds the limiting friction, motion will occur. For two dry surfaces, the limiting friction is a product of the normal reaction force and the coefficient of limiting friction.

Dry Friction Damping (or) Coulomb Damping–Dry friction damping occurs at the interface between two bodies in relative motion with contact. Q371. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 APPSC AE Subordinate Service Civil/Mech. 2016 UKPSC AE, Paper-I 2013
If the number of members in a truss are more than that of a perfect truss. It is known as
A Redundant truss
✓ Correct Answer
B Deficient truss
C Full truss
D General type truss
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
If the number of members in a truss (m) is equal to 2j-3 then it is called perfect truss. Stability and determinacy of truss For 2-D truss m = 2j – 3 → statically determinate (perfect truss) m < 2j–3 → statically determinate but unstable (deficient truss) m > 2j –3 → statically indeterminate (redundant truss)
Q372. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 TSPSC AEE 2015 ISRO Scientist/Engineer (RAC) 29.11.2015 ISRO Scientist/Engineer 24.05.2014 APPSC AE 2012 UKPSC AE Paper-I 2012 ISRO Scientist/Engineer 2009
A perfect frame is that which satisfies the equation (Assume n = No. of members and j = No. of joints)
A n = 3j - 2
B n > 3(j - 1)
C n < 3(j - 1)
D n = (2j - 3)
✓ Correct Answer
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
In general let a frame have j joints and n members. (i) if n = 2j - 3, then the frame is perfect frame. (ii) if n < 2j - 3, then the frame is deficient (Imperfect) frame. (iii) if n > 2j - 3, then the frame is redundant frame.

Q378. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 CGPSC Asstt. Workshop Supt., 17.07.2016
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true for truss design? (i) All loads are applied at the joints. (ii) The members are joined together by smooth pin. (iii) Each truss member acts as single force member.
A Only (i)
B Only (i) and (ii)
✓ Correct Answer
C Only (i) and (iii)
D Only (iii) (e) All (i), (ii) and (iii)
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
A truss is a structure that consists of members organised into connected triangles so that the overall assembly behaves as a single object. A truss is made up of a web of triangles joined together of enables the even distribution of weight and the handling of changing tension and compression without bending or shearing. All loads are applied at the points of member are joined together by smooth pin. Each truss member acts as double force member as equal and opposite force (i.e., either tension or compression) at both ends of the member. Engineering Mechanics 83 YCT

A Radial energy
B Kinetic energy
C Strain energy
✓ Correct Answer
D Circular energy
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
A wound spring has potential energy. The spring does not possesses kinetic energy until it is released and starts to move. Hence energy in the form of potential energy is stored in the spring and when it is unwound it transfers its to energy to the moving parts in the form of kinetic energy. Strain energy is a form of potential energy stored in the material.

Q594. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 KPCL AE 2016
The total energy possessed by a system of moving bodies is_____
A Varies according to the direction of movement
B Constant at any point in time
✓ Correct Answer
C Hyperbolically decreasing over time
D None of these
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
The total energy possessed by a system of moving bodies is constant any point in time. Total mechanical energy is the energy possessed by object due to either its motion or its stored energy of position. The total amount of mechanical energy is merely the sum of these two form of energy. Note-Commission is right answer option (b or d), but actual correct answer is option (b).

Q601. [Engineering Mechanics] 🌐 CIL MT 26.03.2017
If a particle is in static equilibrium, then the work done by the system of force acting on that particle is:
A Negative
B Infinity
C Zero
✓ Correct Answer
D Positive
Book Official Solution & Derivation:
Static equilibrium is a state in which the net force and net torque acted upon the system is zero. In other words, both linear momentum and angular momentum of the system are conserved.
